---
title: "E1. model.json"
---

Place the provided default `model.json` in `PIPELINE_REFDATA_DIR` so the
pipeline has a working attribute and observation model from day one. Once
that's working, swap in a site-specific `model.json` (see the callout below)
whenever you're ready.

::: {.callout-note}
## Building a site-specific model.json

**MSMDAD** is BigPicture's mandatory minimum attribute set. **MetaFlex** covers
optional extensions. To build a `model.json` tailored to your site, browse and
select from both in the
[bpmetrics-config browser](https://bpmetrics-config.tools.balsever.se/), then
use its **"Current Selection"** panel to **"Also export as model.json
(SlideTap)"**. This produces a SlideTap-ready `model.json` directly — place
the downloaded file in `PIPELINE_REFDATA_DIR` in place of the default, and
restart the stack (see the callout below) to pick it up.

Only want the MSMDAD floor for **entity** attributes (case, specimen, block,
slide, image, …), with none of your own on top? Put `{}` in `model.json`.
Those entity attributes are compiled into the pipeline itself, so `{}`
declares nothing extra and still gives you that floor.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## `{}` declares no observation models — check your mappers first

Unlike entities, SlideTap has **no built-in floor for observations**: an
empty `model.json` declares zero observation models, full stop. If any
mapper in your `mappers.xlsx` maps into an observation — a diagnosis or
other pathology code is the normal case, and it counts even though the code
itself is part of MSMDAD — that observation must still be declared by hand
in `model.json`, or mapper injection for it fails silently at boot and every
item using it comes up unmapped, with no error visible in the UI. The
provided default `model.json` above already declares a working `diagnose`
observation as an example. Unless you are certain none of your mappers
touch an observation, start from that file rather than `{}`.
:::

## Place the default file

Run `make setup-refdata` to copy the default `model.json` into your refdata
directory:

```bash
make setup-refdata
```

Expected output (files not yet present):

```
Setting up refdata in: ./data/refdata
Copying mappers.xlsx from bigpicture-slidetap/tests/test_data...
Copying model.json from bigpicture-slidetap/tests/test_data...

Refdata contents:
  mappers.xlsx (9.0K)
  model.json (3.6K)

✓ Setup complete
```

If both files were already present from a previous run:

```
Setting up refdata in: ./data/refdata
✓ mappers.xlsx found
✓ model.json found

Refdata contents:
  mappers.xlsx (9.0K)
  model.json (3.6K)

✓ Setup complete
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Verify

Confirm both refdata files are in place:

```bash
ls ./data/refdata/
```

Expected output:

```
mappers.xlsx  model.json
```

`make doctor` checks all preflight conditions including certificates and
credentials that have not been created yet. Run the full `make doctor` check
at [G. Preflight + boot](boot.qmd) once all prerequisites are in place.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Already have the stack running? This needs a restart to take effect
Editing `model.json` in `PIPELINE_REFDATA_DIR` isn't picked up until the
stack restarts — see [When do I need to
restart?](boot.qmd#when-do-i-need-to-restart) for the command and why.
:::

## Required and optional attributes

Every attribute definition in `model.json` — inside an observation's
`statement.attributes`, or an entity's `additional_attributes` — is
**required by default**. At export, SlideTap checks that every required
attribute has a value; an observation missing one fails the export (see
[If something goes wrong](run-submission.qmd#if-something-goes-wrong) in
H. Run a submission test).

To make an attribute optional, add `"optional": true` to its **existing**
object in `model.json` — this is the only line you add, everything else in
the object stays as-is:

```json
{
  "attribute_type": "code",
  "tag": "diagnose",
  "optional": true
}
```

This is an edit to the reference data file itself, so it needs the same
restart as any other `model.json` change — see the callout above.

::: {.callout-note}
## Editing an MSMDAD attribute's optional flag

The bpmetrics-config export declares **MSMDAD** attributes in `model.json`
alongside your site's own extensions, and SlideTap dedupes any collision with
an entity's fixed attribute on ingest. Still, don't hand-edit an MSMDAD
attribute's entry directly: re-select it in the bpmetrics-config browser and
re-export instead, so the whole file keeps coming from one source and stays
in sync with your selection. If you're not sure whether the attribute named
in an error is part of the MSMDAD floor or your own extension, ask
[Support](../support.qmd) before changing `model.json`.
:::

## Sample relations and cardinality

Besides attributes and observations, `model.json` describes the **sample
chain** — how a biological being, its cases, specimens, blocks and slides hang
together, and how many of each are allowed at every link. Each link is a
*relation*, and each relation carries two keys that set its **cardinality**:
how many items the link permits on either side.

| Key | Constrains |
|---|---|
| `parents` | How many parents a child may have |
| `children` | How many children a parent may have |

So on the specimen → block relation, `parents` is how many specimens one block
may come from, and `children` is how many blocks one specimen may yield.

Both keys take one of four values, and these four are the whole set:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `one` | Exactly one — 1..1 |
| `zero_or_one` | At most one — 0..1 |
| `one_or_more` | At least one — 1..* |
| `zero_or_more` | Any number, none included — 0..* |

### Two different limits: the standard, and your model

Before the table, one distinction that decides how to read it. Cardinality is
set in two independent places, and they do not agree:

- **The metadata standard** — MSMDAD and the MetaFlex XSDs — is what your
  exported bundle is validated against at
  [I. Validate](validate.qmd). It applies no matter what your `model.json`
  says, and you cannot loosen it.
- **`model.json`** is what SlideTap enforces while you curate, before export.
  It can be *stricter* than the standard, and by default in two places it is.

Where they differ, SlideTap will stop you building something the standard would
in fact have accepted. That is worth knowing before you conclude your data
does not fit BigPicture.

### What the standard allows

From the MetaFlex sample and image schemas:

| Reference | Link | Allowed |
|---|---|---|
| `BIOLOGICAL_BEING_REF` | Case → Biological being | exactly 1 |
| `EXTRACTED_FROM_REF` | Specimen → Biological being | exactly 1 |
| `PART_OF_CASE_REF` | Specimen → Case | 0 or 1 |
| `SAMPLED_FROM_REF` | Block → Specimens | **1 or more** |
| `CREATED_FROM_REF` | Slide → Block | exactly 1 |
| `IMAGE_OF` | WSI → Slides | **1 or more** |

The two bold rows are the ones that matter. A block may be sampled from
**several specimens** — the schema calls `BlockType` "a part or a collection of
parts of one or many Specimens" — and nothing in MSMDAD or the XSDs requires
those specimens to come from the same biological being. There are no
cross-entity key or assertion constraints in the schemas at all. **So at the
standard's level, a block can carry more than one biological being.** Likewise
one image may be of several slides, as a macro image over a whole case is.

### What SlideTap's built-in model enforces

SlideTap's own model is tighter. These are the cardinalities in force when you
run with an empty `{}` `model.json`, or with no `model.json` at all:

| Relation | Link | `parents` | `children` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Specimens | Biological being → Specimens | `one` | `one_or_more` |
| Cases | Biological being → Cases | `one` | `one_or_more` |
| Part of case | Case → Specimens | `zero_or_one` | `one_or_more` |
| Sampling to block | Specimen → Blocks | `one` | `one_or_more` |
| Sampling to slide | Block → Slides | `one` | `one_or_more` |
| BpImage of slide | Slide → WSI | `samples`: `one` | `images`: `one_or_more` |

Read that as: every specimen, case, block and slide belongs to **exactly one**
parent, and each parent must have **at least one** child. The one loosening is
*Part of case* — a specimen need not belong to a case at all, but if it does,
it belongs to just one.

Note the two rows that are stricter than the standard: *Sampling to block* sets
`parents` to `one`, so SlideTap will not let a block come from more than one
specimen even though MetaFlex permits it; and *BpImage of slide* sets `samples`
to `one` for the same reason. **If your blocks really are sampled from several
specimens, this is the relation to override** — see below.

The last row is a slide-to-image relation rather than a sample-to-sample one,
so its two keys are named `samples` and `images` instead of `parents` and
`children`. They mean the same thing in the same order.

::: {.callout-warning}
## The shipped `model.json` uses superseded keys, and they are ignored

The `model.json` that `make setup-refdata` copies out of the pipeline's test
data still spells cardinality with the old `min_parents` / `max_parents` /
`min_children` / `max_children` keys. Those are **no longer fields on the
model**, and SlideTap silently discards keys it does not recognise — no
warning, no boot error.

The practical effect: every sample relation in that file falls back to the
field default, which is `zero_or_more` on **both** sides. A pipeline started
from the shipped file enforces **no cardinality constraints at all** on the
sample chain — not the `one` / `zero_or_one` values in the table above.

Note that this only bites because the file *declares* the relations. An empty
`{}` `model.json` leaves them out entirely and you get the built-in values in
the table; the shipped file names them and so replaces the built-ins, and the
values it means to set are the ones being dropped. The two starting points
you're offered therefore behave differently, and the more complete-looking one
constrains less.

None of this affects validation at
[I. Validate](validate.qmd) — the standard's limits still apply to the exported
bundle either way. What you lose is SlideTap catching a shape problem during
curation, while it is still cheap to fix.
:::

### Overriding a relation

Set `parents` or `children` on the relation you want to change. Everything
else in the relation object stays as it is — you are adding two keys (and, if
you're starting from the shipped file, removing the four superseded ones from
that relation).

The likeliest real reason to do this is the mismatch noted above: your blocks
are sampled from more than one specimen, which the standard allows but
SlideTap's built-in model does not. This relaxes *Sampling to block* to match
what MetaFlex permits.

```json
{
  "specimen": {
    "uid": "b1e71da2-c235-401f-ae6b-42e8b32fd5b9",
    "block": {
      "uid": "2702fc6b-6ac5-4191-8230-82d976815ebb",
      "name": "Sampling to block",
      "parent_uid": "b1e71da2-c235-401f-ae6b-42e8b32fd5b9",
      "child_uid": "cf80a5f5-6ffe-44c4-bfc3-79c8861cf6e3",
      "parent_title": "Specimen",
      "child_title": "Blocks",
      "parents": "one_or_more",
      "children": "one_or_more"
    }
  }
}
```

Relations are grouped under the entity they describe, and the inner key names
the entity at the other end — so `specimen.block` is the specimen-to-block
link. Any relation can be overridden this way.

Like every other `model.json` edit, this takes effect only after the stack
restarts — see [When do I need to
restart?](boot.qmd#when-do-i-need-to-restart).

## If something goes wrong

**`FAIL: model.json missing from ...`** — run `make setup-refdata` again and
confirm `model.json` appears in `PIPELINE_REFDATA_DIR`.

**`Warning: model.json not found in bigpicture-slidetap/tests/test_data`** —
the pipeline submodule was not initialised. Run:

```bash
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

then retry `make setup-refdata`.

**Export reverts to "Completed" with no error, and an observation is missing
a coded attribute (e.g. `diagnose`)** — that attribute has no `"optional":
true` flag in `model.json`, so it is required by default (see [Required and
optional attributes](#required-and-optional-attributes) above). Either supply
the missing value for that observation before re-exporting, or mark the
attribute optional in `model.json` and restart the stack. Full symptom,
including why Curate can miss this, and where to find the underlying error:
[H. Run a submission test](run-submission.qmd#if-something-goes-wrong).
